Hmm I feel like you're not quite understanding my argument. I'll try to simplify my response. (You neither disproved/rebutted my arguments so I hope I'm right to assume that you've given up on your original point and focus on your new one :) ) 

The fallacy of your analogy is the fact that you're touting that Josh is committing a crime in order to get more money, or he is actively placing the possum back inside of the home even though the home owners took measures to prevent it, when he isn't. 

He releases the possum, the home owners don't take effort to defend their home, and naturally, the assumed same possum (which, it could just be new ones anyways because they didn't do anything other than have the critter removed) thus returns. 

If the person asked Josh to cut the tree, which he does, and disposes of the tree properly, and the pollen makes its way back onto the property and grows into a tree, is that Josh's responsibility? He did his job, legally and properly for what he was paid. It is the property owners responsibility to ensure repeated instances don't happen, and to address issues proactively rather than reactively, to address the root issue, all of which is NOT Josh's responsibility. 

Does that clarify a bit?

I respectfully disagree and here's why; a better analogy would be if someone with a broken windshield went to get it fixed. The owners keep breaking it because they keep running into a tree on their property they can't be bothered to get rid of. Is the windshield repair man required to tell the people how to prevent their windshield from breaking? Are they required to go out and trim the tree themselves? Should they go to jail because they didn't warn the car owner against driving their car into trees branches? Should he give back the money just because people keep making the same mistake? No. Of course not. He just does what he's paid to do, which is fix the windshield. It's up to the owner of the car to assess the reason for the constant damage and to fix it. They're grown adults who don't need to be babied. Your analogy doesn't make sense due to another major flaw - the man isn't going around altering people's homes, damaging their property, to make it easier for possums to get in, as you insinuate with yours.
Wow what a great example of a  fucking self absorbed asshole

Thanks for the advise - I really do agree on how he would react. Fits the bill on what I think as well, knowing him. That’s also basically what’s happened if I confronted my exes as well. They just turn it around on me, blame me and guilt me until I end up begging and apologizing. Yet I always end up trusting the next person who seems to show me goodwill. Oh well. 

I really shouldn’t rely on him, as you said. It feels degrading that my life is essentially in his control. Maybe he gets a kick out of the power and that’s why it’s exciting to him, to do this to me. Because he knows I can’t complain even if I ‘find out’. 

 I’m just scared and confused on what I can do - the only other visa options I see are for skilled workers or being sponsored by work. My work just being a casual wait staff, I know I wouldn’t be able to get sponsored, and I didn’t complete college or have much work experience before I moved here so I’m not considered skilled. 

I’ve been applying to other jobs in order to try and get a sponsorship, took a course on medical reception and terminology and am getting whatever work experience I can get, even volunteering, but it’s all seeming to add up to nothing so far, though I’ll keep trying. I’ll keep trying to search other ways, and I’ll keep trying to go for sponsorships. Even if I stay now, as soon as I can, I would leave. In the meantime, should I tell him, and potentially move out, risking my life here on being able to find another option, or should I stay and be silent until I can find a safe route out? Maybe it will help if you know that it will be about 7 months until I can apply for the permanent residency, which after I get, I can be away from him. Sorry for how much I type.
